🇲🇽📊 <u>INFLATION TICKS UP TO 3.42%, CORE KEEPS COOLING</u>

Mexico’s annual inflation rose to 3.42% in the first half of September from 3.26%, Inegi reported — pushed by tomatoes, up 22.79% in just two weeks. But core inflation, which strips out volatile prices, eased to 3.79% from 3.83%, and the headline stays inside Banxico’s 3% ±1 target band. Services remain the sticky part at 4.33%, per El Economista.

🇲🇽💉 <u>MEXICO APPROVES THE TWICE-A-YEAR HIV SHOT</u>

Mexico’s health regulator Cofepris approved lenacapavir for HIV pre-exposure prophylaxis — the long-acting injection given just twice a year that the WHO recommended in 2025. Mexico joins Brazil, the United States and the European Union in using it, cleared on evidence of quality, safety and efficacy. It becomes a new option for people at high risk and for those living with HIV.

🚨🇲🇽 <u>AYOTZINAPA, 12 YEARS ON: NEW LINES, NEW ARRESTS</u>

On the eve of the 12th anniversary of the disappearance of the 43 Ayotzinapa students, President Sheinbaum announced that on Monday, September 28 the government will present new lines of investigation, search progress and new arrests. Special prosecutor Mauricio Pazarán and Deputy Minister Arturo Medina will lay out the scientific evidence — including phone activity from the night of September 26–27, 2014, lines previous investigations never pursued. The families already know part of it: they met with Sheinbaum a month ago. Tomorrow they march.

🇲🇽📉 <u>TABASCO HOMICIDES DOWN 54%</u>

Tabasco’s daily homicide average fell 54% — from 3.5 at its November 2024 peak to 1.6 in August 2026 — reported Marcela Figueroa, head of Mexico’s public security secretariat (SESNSP). Comparing January–August, kidnapping is down 75% and femicide 50%; violent car theft fell 51% from the peak. Since October 2024, Harfuch’s Security Cabinet counts more than 6,500 arrests, 2,000 firearms and 13 tons of drugs seized in the state.

🇲🇽✈️ <u>59.7 MILLION VISITORS, FIVE TOURISM RECORDS</u>

Mexico broke five tourism records in January–July 2026: 59.7 million international visitors, up 7%, spending 21.743 billion dollars. Overnight tourists grew 4.5% to 28.9 million — beating the 3% global average — and cruise arrivals jumped 13.6% to 7.4 million. Tourism Secretary Josefina Rodríguez Zamora reported 140 new air routes, 64 of them international. Nearly 40% of foreign travelers now come for culture and sport before sun and beach.

🇲🇽🌎 <u>MEXICO TO THE UN: THE CHARTER IS ALREADY IN OUR CONSTITUTION</u>

Foreign Minister Roberto Velasco took Mexico’s sovereignty doctrine to the UN General Assembly: Mexico “has shown that a country can cooperate closely and respectfully with its partners and at the same time fully assert its sovereignty.” He rejected the embargo on Cuba, pledged to keep sending humanitarian aid to the island, reaffirmed Mexico’s recognition of the State of Palestine and called for a renewed UN. “Mexico does not need to adapt its foreign policy to the UN Charter — it has it written in its Constitution.”

text: 🇲🇽🔍 Tabasco: homicides down 54%. "Those are the two arms. On one hand, attending to young people, attending to the people… and on the other hand, zero impunity." — Presidenta Claudia Sheinbaum, Villahermosa The average daily homicide rate in Tabasco fell 54% from its November 2024 peak to August 2026. High-impact crimes are down 18% from 2024 to 2026 and violent car theft is down 51%. Since October 2024, more than 6,500 people have been arrested in the state, with 2,000 firearms and 13 tons of drugs seized.

🇲🇽🌎 "The economic competition that exists does not have to generate rivalries between countries." "The rivalry between two important nations such as China and the United States generates uncertainty in the world, and what Mexico has always sought is peace and cooperation for development." — Presidenta Claudia Sheinbaum, on Xi Jinping's remarks Asked about Xi Jinping's call for a peaceful US–China relationship and healthy competition, she noted Xi said China's development does not contradict "making America greater," President Trump's slogan. She will attend the APEC summit in China in November, since Mexico hosts APEC in 2028.

🇲🇽🌎 "On others, they depend on our sovereignty, and of course, there we are not going to give in." "So of course we are interested in economic integration, but always with sovereignty." — Presidenta Claudia Sheinbaum, on the trade talks with the US Mexico is seeking no new tariffs and lower existing ones on steel and automobiles. She noted that no country in the world buys more from the United States than Mexico. Economy Secretary Marcelo Ebrard will be in Washington again on Monday.
